title: Calculate Score After Performing Instructions
summary: Given two arrays, instructions and values of size n, simulate a process starting at index 0 with a score of 0.
statement: Given two arrays, instructions and values of size n, simulate a process starting at index 0 with a score of 0. Follow rules: if 'add', add values[i] to score and move to next instruction; if 'jump', move to the instruction at index (i + values[i]) without changing score. The process ends if out of bounds or revisiting an instruction. Return the final score.
constraints: instructions and values have equal length up to 100,000.
At add, add the aligned value and advance one; at jump, move by the aligned signed offset without changing score.
Stop before executing an out-of-bounds or previously executed index, and return the score.
reference_solution:
def calculate_instruction_score(instructions, values):
    visited=set();index=0;score=0
    while 0<=index<len(values) and index not in visited:
        visited.add(index)
        if instructions[index]=='add':score+=values[index];index+=1
        else:index+=values[index]
    return score

def calculate_instruction_score(instructions, values):
    visited=set();index=0;score=0
    while 0<=index<len(values) and index not in visited:
        visited.add(index)
        if instructions[index]=='add':score+=values[index];index+=1
        else:index=values[index]
    return score
hints: The process is deterministic, so the first repeated index begins a loop and must stop the simulation.
Track executed indices in a set and apply exactly one rule at each new in-bounds position.
While the index is valid and unseen, mark it; either add and increment or jump by the signed offset.
Each instruction executes at most once, and the loop condition matches both specified stopping conditions.
